what: Repeat/evidence policy for GPU session #2 (R4 README R10/§11, plus the six human locks taken at the pre-GPU documentation cleanup).
status_note: Signed off by the human as locks D-CLEAN-1..6 ahead of Hard Stop R-DOC. Superseded the earlier PROPOSED state of 2026-08-19. metrics.classification.RepeatPolicy mirrors the `policy` block below rather than hard-coding values elsewhere, so the numbers stay a recorded human decision.

human_locks.D-CLEAN-1: 1A -- three independent repeats per headline lambda; final classification requires agreement; a 2-1 split is UNCERTAIN, never a majority verdict.
human_locks.D-CLEAN-2: 2B -- N=4000 is the authorized headline evidence size. N=5000 is NOT authorized. An unresolved crossing is reported as a breach interval.
human_locks.D-CLEAN-3: 3A -- repeats from different vLLM process epochs may not be combined into one final classification family.
human_locks.D-CLEAN-4: 4A -- the 60s warmup boundary is frozen into the exact-N schedules and validated during Tier A. Post-hoc warmup re-filtering of headline sidecars is not a valid resolution.
human_locks.D-CLEAN-5: 5A -- scout lambda 1/2/4/8, with 0.5 and 16 pre-authorized as fallback. No other lambda may be invented on the meter.
human_locks.D-CLEAN-6: 6A -- Week 2 is not closed until the controlled Poisson headline, the natural-random secondary, the steady-arrival reference and the adversarial scenario are accounted for. Only the controlled Poisson workload defines the headline breach.

rationale.min_valid_repeats: Three is the smallest number that can show disagreement AS disagreement: with two, a split is a tie and there is no way to tell which run was unusual.
rationale.require_unanimous: Near the SLO a 2-1 split IS the finding -- the point is unstable. Taking the majority would convert an honest UNCERTAIN into a verdict, which is the failure the first session already made once.
rationale.majority_vote: Stated as an explicit false rather than left implicit, because 'unanimous' and 'majority' are the same word to a hurried reader on a meter.
rationale.n_per_run: Smallest grid candidate reaching a <=5% per-run classification-flip rate on the conservative 2-RPS bootstrap source (R3 evidence package 4.1).
rationale.n_max: Structural: the pinned corpus holds 5,000 prompts, so a larger canonical multiset would require repeating prompts, which is not neutral with prefix caching and is forbidden.
rationale.max_repeats_authorized: Three at N=4,000 is ~5.4h of drive time in the worst-case lambda set. Beyond that the session length itself becomes the dominant risk (spot preemption), not the statistics.
rationale.max_ttft_p99_spread_ms: Left null deliberately. Spread is RECORDED for every point; gating on a threshold nobody has calibrated would invent a rule, and unanimity already catches the case that matters.
rationale.cross_process_epoch_combination: A vLLM restart (spot preemption is the realistic cause) resets the engine state the repeats were meant to hold constant. Mixing epochs would let process-initialization variance enter one repeat and not the others, silently, at exactly the boundary where the verdict is decided.
rationale.warmup_boundary_s: Frozen into the materialized exact-N schedules: N arrivals are materialized at or after this boundary. It is validated against the Tier A transient BEFORE Tier B is driven.
rationale.post_hoc_warmup_refilter: Valid under the superseded fixed-duration design, invalid for the redesigned exact-N headline: filtering past the frozen boundary discards canonical arrivals and leaves fewer than N measured samples. metrics/headline_point.py refuses it. If 60s proves insufficient, the schedules are REGENERATED at a larger boundary, offline.
rationale.unresolved_boundary: An interval is a legitimate final answer. A <=1% per-run flip rate would need N ~ 7,500, above n_max, so escalating on the meter cannot reach it.

n5000.why_not: Locked as D-CLEAN-2 (2B). The earlier proposal left this open as at-most-one re-drive of a single UNCERTAIN boundary lambda at N=5,000. The human closed it: if N=4,000 cannot resolve the crossing under the unanimity rule, the answer is a breach interval, not a bigger meter bill.

escalation.note: No escalation of any kind is authorized for GPU session #2. This field was `null` while the policy was PROPOSED; it is now an explicit false.

scout.evidence_class: DIAGNOSTIC -- locates the crossing region, never enters classification

preauthorized_fallback.if_fallback_still_fails_to_bracket: STOP and return to human review

secondary_scope.execution_order_note: Adversarial runs last -- it deliberately drives the replica toward saturation.
secondary_scope.interpretation_rule: Secondary scenarios may support interpretation of the headline breach. They may never redefine it.

stop_condition.rule: If the crossing is still unresolved once the authorized ceiling is reached, report breach interval = (highest defensible UNDER lambda, lowest defensible OVER lambda] and stop.
never: escalate N beyond 4,000 for GPU session #2
repeat corpus prompts to manufacture a larger N
add unplanned repeats on the meter
take a majority verdict from split repeats
combine repeats from different vLLM process epochs
resolve an insufficient warmup by re-filtering headline sidecars after the run
invent scout lambda values beyond the pre-authorized fallback
